x: The individual race was won easily by "Lofty" Holden, of Cambridge H., and our first man home was Bob Taylor, 17th, our other scorers being Mick Porter, 27; John Burr, 32; Ray Tooby, 38; Len Bishop, 57, and George Stace, 61.

In fairness to the Bishop brothers we must point out that Alan only came into our team at the last moment owing to the non-arrival of Mick Porter, while Len was spiked early in the race, and this must have affected his running.

Wal Wortley showed a most welcome return to form and it was pleasing to see our late member Mick Porter, now of Manchester, in such good shape. we did however, suffer a severe misfortune when Bert Jordan retired with tendon trouble after 15 miles.
Mick Porter, an old member of the cross-country section, has become the proud father of twins - making 4 children in all. Mick sends his regards to all his Belgrave friends.
Mick Porter and Lew Bush also ran well as did J.H.Braggington, who is a first season runner over the country.
We hear that Mike Porter, an active Belgravian in the late 1940's and early 1950's, is now treasurer of the Northern Veterans' A.C. and still clocking around 64 minutes for ten miles.
Bob Taylor ran well to finish 20th, and Mick Porter 27th also did well. (Other members: 63.E.Stimpson; 70.J.McDonald; 73.R.W.Tobin; 85.R.J.Wolton; 127.A.
One of the first to reply was Mike Porter who was a member of Belgrave from 1948 to 1953 before moving back to Manchester. He wrote "I have many happy memories of Belgrave.
